patch.summary:
Thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.

Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge. Choose Five9 only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/E” rather than Ooma's shape. Choose Ooma only if your buying job matches “SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.” rather than Five9's shape. Workflow advantage: Five9 leans contact-center, customer-messaging; Ooma leans business-phone. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Same category, different company size — Both sit in business-communications, but documented company-size audiences diverge.
- Positioning: Five9 is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/Enterprise quote — 50-seat minimum.; Ooma is SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro Plus $29.95 — no annual lock-in..
- Company-size focus: Five9 (mid-market, enterprise) vs Ooma (solo, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Five9-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging vs Ooma-leaning business-phone.
- Researched limits: Five9 — 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Ooma — SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited.

Limitations — Five9: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Digital is non-voice; Core is the published voice+digital entry; Ooma: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited; Call queues, CRM and auto-dialer require Pro Plus.

Poor-fit cases: Five9 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers · Ooma is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SMS allotments are account-wide caps (e.g. Pro ~250/mo) — not per-user unlimited · Avoid Five9 if you actually need Ooma's motion (SMB VoIP (Ooma Office) — Essentials from $19.95/user/mo monthly; Pro $24.95; Pro)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
